questions.question: If the selling price of a bed is 2-times of initial, then the profit is 7-times of initial. Find the initial profit percentage (in %)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let initial **Selling Price (SP₁)** be 1 and **Cost Price (CP)** be x.

Initial Profit (P₁) = 1 − x. New Selling Price (SP₂) = 2.

New Profit (P₂) = 2 − x. According to question: P₂ = 7 × P₁.

2 − x = 7(1 − x) ⇒ 2 − x = 7 − 7x ⇒ 6x = 5 ⇒ x = 5/6.

Initial Profit % = [(1 − 5/6) ÷ (5/6)] × 100 = (1/5) × 100 = 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → SPₙₑw = 2 × SPₒₗd | Pₙₑw = 7 × Pₒₗd.
Formulas: Profit = SP − CP | Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ff7b99b19f26dc639053de6a35f554f364eea03b1074e83fbd6b81c87a6f502f.png] 
⇒ Let CP = C, SPᵢₙᵢₜᵢₐₗ = S.
⇒ Pᵢₙᵢₜᵢₐₗ = S − C.
⇒ Pₙₑw = 2S − C.
⇒ According to condition: 2S − C = 7(S − C).
⇒ 2S − C = 7S − 7C.
⇒ 6C = 5S ⇒ S/C = 6/5.
⇒ Profit% = [(6 − 5) ÷ 5] × 100 = 1/5 × 100 = 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss relationship

If the **Cost Price** remains constant, any change in the **Selling Price** results in a direct change in the absolute profit amount by the same difference.

Profit Percentage Formula

Profit% is always calculated on the **Cost Price** unless stated otherwise: Profit% = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100.</p

questions.question: A dealer purchased a ceiling fan for ₹66,000. He allows a discount of 56% on its marked price and still gains 69%. Find the marked price of the ceiling fan.

MP ÷ 66,000 = (100 + 69) ÷ (100 − 56) = 169 ÷ 44.

MP = (66,000 × 169) ÷ 44 = 1,500 × 169.

MP = 2,53,500.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,53,500.**

⇒ 1,11,540 = MP × 44 ÷ 100.
⇒ MP = (1,11,540 × 100) ÷ 44.
⇒ MP = 2,535 × 100 = ₹2,53,500.

Marked Price & Discount

The **Marked Price (MP)** is the price listed by the seller, and **Discount** is always calculated on this MP to arrive at the Selling Price.

CP-MP Relation

The direct formula **CP/MP = (100 − D%)/(100 + P%)** is a very efficient way to solve problems involving both discount and profit percentages.

questions.question: Which court in the subordinate judiciary has unlimited pecuniary jurisdiction in civil cases?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Judge of District Court**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **District Court** serves as the principal court of original jurisdiction in civil matters in the subordinate judiciary system in India.
 
• The District Court is presided over by the **District Judge**, who has the authority to hear civil cases with **unlimited pecuniary jurisdiction** unless restricted by specific legislative provisions.
 
• These courts handle a wide range of civil disputes, including property disputes, matrimonial cases, and contractual disagreements, among others.
 
• District Courts are established by state governments in India for every district or group of districts, as per the **Code of Civil Procedure, 1908**.
 
• The decisions of the District Court can be appealed to the **High Court** of the respective state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pecuniary Jurisdiction:**

 
 
• Pecuniary jurisdiction refers to the monetary value of cases that a particular court is authorized to hear and adjudicate.
 
• In India, lower courts like the Court of Munsiff typically have limited pecuniary jurisdiction, while District Courts have no upper monetary limit unless restricted by state laws.
 
 
 
• **Hierarchy of Civil Courts:**
 
 
• The hierarchy of civil courts in India includes the Court of Munsiff, Civil Judge (Junior Division), Civil Judge (Senior Division), and District Courts.
 
• Above the subordinate courts, civil matters can be escalated to the High Courts and, in some cases, the Supreme Court of India.
 
 
 
• **Small Causes Court:**
 
 
• Small Causes Courts deal with cases related to small monetary disputes, typically with a value below a certain threshold, which varies by state.
 
• They lack jurisdiction over cases involving property disputes or other significant civil matters.
 
 
 
• **Nyaya Panchayat:**
 
 
• Nyaya Panchayats are grassroots-level judicial bodies in rural areas that handle minor civil and criminal cases.
 
• They focus on delivering speedy and cost-effective justice but have limited jurisdiction and authority.
 
 
 
• **Code of Civil Procedure, 1908:**
 
 
• This is the primary legislation governing the functioning and procedures of civil courts in India.
 
• It defines the jurisdiction, powers, and structure of courts, including the District Courts and subordinate courts.

questions.question: Rakesh’s salary is ₹12,000 per month. He spends ₹6,000 on house rent, ₹3,000 on bills and the rest of the amount is his monthly savings. Find his savings (in ₹) in a year, if in the month of his birthday, he spent his complete monthly savings for the birthday celebration

**Monthly Savings** = 12,000 − (6,000 + 3,000) = ₹3,000.

Savings are done for 11 months only (as 1 month savings spent on birthday).

**Yearly Savings** = 3,000 × 11 = ₹33,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹33,000.**

questions.question: If the roots of the quadratic equation k x ^ 2 - 4x + 1 = 0 are real and equal, what is the value of k?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For a **quadratic equation** to have **real and equal roots**, its **discriminant (D)** must be zero.

D = b² − 4ac = 0

In the equation kx² − 4x + 1 = 0, we have (−4)² − 4 × k × 1 = 0.

16 − 4k = 0 ⇒ 4k = 16 ⇒ k = 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The **quadratic equation** is kx² − 4x + 1 = 0.

**Formula Used:**

A quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0 has **real and equal roots** if:

**Discriminant (D) = b² − 4ac = 0**

**Calculations:**

Comparing the given equation with the standard form ax² + bx + c = 0:

a = k, b = −4, and c = 1

Substitute these values into the discriminant formula:

⇒ (−4)² − 4 × (k) × (1) = 0

⇒ 16 − 4k = 0

⇒ 4k = 16

⇒ k = 16 ÷ 4

⇒ k = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

**__Additional Information__**

Nature of Roots

The nature of roots is determined by D = b² − 4ac. If D > 0, roots are **real and distinct**; if D = 0, roots are **real and equal**; if D < 0, roots are **complex/imaginary**.

Discriminant Formula

For any quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0, the **discriminant** is given by D = b² − 4ac.

Standard Quadratic Form

A **standard quadratic equation** is represented as ax² + bx + c = 0, where a ≠ 0.</p

questions.question: The longitudinal valleys between the lesser Himalayas and the Shiwaliks are called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Duns**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Duns** are longitudinal valleys situated between the **Lesser Himalayas** (or Middle Himalayas) and the **Shiwalik** range.
 
• They are formed due to the folding of sedimentary rocks during the Himalayan orogeny (mountain-building process).
 
• Examples of prominent duns include **Dehradun**, **Kotli Dun**, and **Patli Dun**.
 
• These valleys are often fertile and support agriculture, making them important for the local economy.
 
• The term "dun" is derived from the Hindi word “doon,” which means a valley.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lesser Himalayas:**

 
 
• The Lesser Himalayas, also called the **Himachal**, are located north of the Shiwaliks and south of the Greater Himalayas.
 
• They are composed of metamorphic and sedimentary rocks and are known for their rugged terrain and deep valleys.
 
 
 
• **Shiwalik Range:**
 
 
• The Shiwaliks are the outermost range of the Himalayas and are made up of unconsolidated sediments brought down by rivers.
 
• This range is prone to erosion and is characterized by steep slopes.
 
 
 
• **Himalayan Orogeny:**
 
 
• The Himalayas were formed due to the collision of the Indian Plate with the Eurasian Plate around 50 million years ago.
 
• This tectonic activity caused the folding and upliftment of sedimentary rocks, leading to the formation of ranges and valleys like duns.
 
 
 
• **Other Types of Valleys:**
 
 
• **Doabs:** Land between two rivers, typically used in the Indo-Gangetic Plains (e.g., Punjab's doabs).
 
• **Meanders:** Curved bends in a river channel, primarily formed in its lower course.
 
• **Khadars:** Fertile alluvial soil regions formed by river deposition during floods, often found in the Indo-Gangetic Plains.

questions.question: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2,000 at 6% per annum rate of interest for the period from 3 February 2023 to 17 April 2023.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the total days: **Feb (25) + Mar (31) + Apr (17) = 73 days**.

Since 73 days is exactly **1/5** of a year (73/365), calculate 1/5 of the annual interest.

Annual Interest = 6% of ₹2,000 = ₹120.

Simple Interest for the period = 120 ÷ 5 = **₹24**.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = **₹2,000**

Rate (R) = **6% per annum**

Period: **3 February 2023** to **17 April 2023**

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/88219710fae221590b332de528c817a1f19e7b211de52b07af76ab3537616a13.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Number of days in February = 28 − 3 = **25 days** (2023 is a non-leap year)

⇒ Number of days in March = **31 days**

⇒ Number of days in April = **17 days**

⇒ Total days (T) = 25 + 31 + 17 = **73 days**

⇒ Time in years = 73 ÷ 365 = **1/5 year**

⇒ SI = (2000 × 6 × 1/5) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = (2000 × 6) ÷ 500

⇒ SI = 4 × 6 = **24**

**∴ The correct answer is ₹24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

While calculating the number of days, the day on which money is deposited is usually excluded and the day on which money is withdrawn is included.

Standard Year vs Leap Year

For interest calculations, a standard year is taken as 365 days. If the year is a leap year (divisible by 4), February has 29 days.

Relationship between Amount and SI

The total **Amount (A)** repaid after the period is the sum of the **Principal (P)** and the **Simple Interest (SI)**: A = P + SI.

questions.question: Four numbers are in the ratio of 11 : 19 : 5 : 7 respectively. If the sum of these four numbers is 2289, then what is the sum of the first and the third number?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Ratio sum** = 11 + 19 + 5 + 7 = 42 units

42 units = 2289 → 1 unit = 2289 ÷ 42 = 54.5

**Required sum** (1st + 3rd) = 11 + 5 = 16 units

Sum = 16 × 54.5 = 872

**∴ The correct answer is 872.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7aaf23596bd51fdd3fde3c71154b83d875d8a0fd8d57db0f6385946e66c99221.png] 

**Given:**

Ratio of four numbers = 11 : 19 : 5 : 7

Total Sum = 2289

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the numbers be 11x, 19x, 5x, and 7x.

⇒ Sum = 11x + 19x + 5x + 7x = 42x

⇒ 42x = 2289

⇒ x = 2289 ÷ 42

⇒ x = 54.5

⇒ Sum of 1st and 3rd number = 11x + 5x = 16x

⇒ Required Sum = 16 × 54.5 = 872

**∴ The correct answer is 872.**

**__Additional Information__**

Ratio and Proportion

A **ratio** indicates how many times one number contains another. If a : b = c : d, then a × d = b × c.

Distribution of Quantity

To divide a quantity **S** in the ratio a:b:c, the shares are S × [a/(a+b+c)], S × [b/(a+b+c)], and so on.

Compound Ratio

The **compound ratio** of a:b and c:d is (ac) : (bd). It is used for combining multiple related ratios.</p

questions.question: Jitesh and Kamal can complete a certain piece of work in 5 and 18 days, respectively, They started to work together, and after 3 days, Kamal left. In how many days will Jitesh complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
Total work (LCM of 5 and 18) = 90 units.

Efficiency: **Jitesh** = 18 units/day, **Kamal** = 5 units/day.

Combined work in 3 days = 3 × (18 + 5) = 69 units.

Remaining work = 90 − 69 = 21 units.

Days for Jitesh to finish = 21 ÷ 18 = 7/6 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 7/6 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 **Person** **Days** **Total Work** **Efficiency**
 **Jitesh** 5 90 18
 **Kamal** 18 5
Given: **Jitesh** completes work in 5 days, **Kamal** in 18 days.

Formula: **Remaining Work** = **Total Work** − **Work Done**

⇒ Total work = LCM(5, 18) = 90 units

⇒ Efficiency of **Jitesh** = 90 ÷ 5 = 18 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of **Kamal** = 90 ÷ 18 = 5 units/day

⇒ Work done together in 3 days = 3 × (18 + 5) = 3 × 23 = 69 units

⇒ Remaining work = 90 − 69 = 21 units

⇒ Time taken by **Jitesh** to finish remaining work = 21 ÷ 18

⇒ Time = 7/6 days

**∴ The correct answer is 7/6 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Time Relation

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete the work. Efficiency × Time = Total Work.

Work & Wages

Wages are distributed based on the ratio of work done by each individual, which is the product of their efficiency and time spent working.

Fractional Work Method

If a person does work in 'x' days, work done in 1 day = 1/x. Sum of daily fractions of work gives the total combined efficiency.</p

questions.question: The World Sustainable Development Summit 2025 took place in which city?

The correct answer is __**New Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

• The World Sustainable Development Summit (WSDS) is an annual flagship event organized by **The Energy and Resources Institute (TERI)**.
 
• The WSDS 2025 took place in **New Delhi, India**, continuing the tradition of addressing critical global sustainability challenges.
 
• The summit serves as a platform for global leaders, policymakers, and researchers to deliberate on sustainable development goals and climate action strategies.

questions.question: Which of the following Operating System concepts is most directly involved in ensuring that multiple processes can access and modify files concurrently without causing data corruption?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**File locking mechanisms**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **File locking mechanisms** are designed to ensure data integrity and prevent data corruption when multiple processes access the same file concurrently.
 
• Locks can be applied at different levels, such as **file-level locks** or **record-level locks**, depending on the granularity of the access control required.
 
• File locking ensures that only one process can modify a file at a time, while other processes may be blocked or granted read-only access.
 
• Operating systems like Linux and Windows provide built-in APIs or system calls (e.g., `flock` in Linux) to implement file locking for developers.
 
• Improper implementation of file locking mechanisms can lead to issues like **deadlock** or **livestock**, which require careful handling in concurrent programming.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concurrency in Operating Systems:**

 
 
• Concurrency refers to the ability of an operating system to allow multiple processes or threads to execute simultaneously.
 
• It is managed through mechanisms like process scheduling, synchronization, and file locking.
 
• Concurrency is crucial for improving the efficiency and resource utilization of modern operating systems.
 
 
 
• **Deadlock:**
 
 
• Deadlock occurs when two or more processes are unable to proceed because each is waiting for the other to release a resource.
 
• File locking can sometimes lead to deadlock, which can be mitigated using techniques like timeout-based locking or deadlock detection algorithms.
 
 
 
• **Virtual Memory Management:**
 
 
• Virtual memory allows an operating system to use disk storage to simulate additional RAM, enabling processes to run even when physical memory is limited.
 
• While related to process management, virtual memory does not directly address file access concurrency.
 
 
 
• **Scheduling Algorithms:**
 
 
• Scheduling algorithms determine the order in which processes are executed by the CPU.
 
• Common algorithms include First Come First Serve (FCFS), Shortest Job Next (SJN), and Round Robin (RR).
 
• They do not directly handle file access conflicts but are essential for process management.

questions.question: Which of the following acts of the East India Company formally separated the Legislative and Executive functions of Governor-General’s Council?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Charter Act of 1853**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Charter Act of 1853** was the last in the series of Charter Acts passed by the British Parliament for the governance of India.
 
• This Act formally **separated the legislative and executive functions** of the Governor-General’s Council.
 
• A separate **Legislative Council** was created under this Act, marking the beginning of a distinct legislative machinery in British India.
 
• The Governor-General’s Council now had six members—four executive and two legislative members.
 
• The Act also allowed Indians to be appointed to the Legislative Council for the first time, although their participation was limited.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Charter Act of 1833:**

 
 
• It made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India, centralizing administration.
 
• It ended the commercial operations of the East India Company and made it a purely administrative body.
 
• The Act attempted to introduce open competition for civil services but faced opposition.
 
 
 
• **Key Terminology:**
 
 
• **Governor-General's Council:** The council was an advisory body assisting the Governor-General in administrative and legislative matters.
 
• **Legislative Council:** A body created for enacting laws, distinct from the executive functions of the government.
 
 
 
• **Role of the East India Company:**
 
 
• The East India Company initially held both administrative and commercial powers in India.
 
• The Charter Acts progressively curbed its commercial role and enhanced its administrative authority under British Parliament's control.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Charter Act of 1853:**
 
 
• It marked a step towards modern legislative practices in India.
 
• The Act laid the groundwork for subsequent reforms, including the Indian Councils Act of 1861.

questions.question: Most of the Thar Desert lies in which direction with respect to the Aravalli Hills?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**North-West**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Thar Desert is geographically located to the **North-West of the Aravalli Hills**, which act as a natural barrier influencing its climatic conditions.
 
• The Aravalli Hills, one of the oldest mountain ranges in the world, run from northeast to southwest across northwestern India.
 
• The orientation of the Aravalli Hills significantly affects the wind patterns, leading to the accumulation of desert sand towards the North-West region.
 
• The Thar Desert spans across the Indian states of Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab, and Haryana, with a major portion lying in Rajasthan.
 
• The desert's proximity to the Aravalli Hills helps restrict the eastward expansion of the sandy terrain.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thar Desert:**

 
 
• The Thar Desert, also known as the Great Indian Desert, is the 17th largest desert in the world and the 9th largest subtropical desert.
 
• It covers an area of approximately 200,000 square kilometers, making it the most densely populated desert in the world.
 
• The desert is characterized by extreme temperatures, scarce vegetation, and low precipitation (100-500 mm annually).
 
 
 
• **Aravalli Hills:**
 
 
• The Aravalli Hills are a range of ancient fold mountains extending approximately 692 kilometers across northwest India.
 
• They play a crucial role in determining the local climate and act as a protective barrier against desertification to the east.
 
• The highest peak is Guru Shikhar, located in Mount Abu, Rajasthan, at an elevation of 1,722 meters.
 
 
 
• **Climatic Influence:**
 
 
• The Aravalli Hills influence the monsoon winds, causing the western region to remain arid while the eastern plains receive moderate rainfall.
 
• The desert's location to the northwest of the hills results in its characteristic dry and sandy climate.
 
 
 
• **Flora and Fauna:**
 
 
• The desert supports various drought-resistant plants such as cacti, acacia, and khejri trees.
 
• Wildlife includes species like the Indian gazelle (chinkara), desert fox, and great Indian bustard, which are adapted to arid conditions.

questions.question: The relics of Buddha are found inside which of the following Buddhist architectures?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Stupas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Stupas** are hemispherical structures that serve as repositories for sacred relics, typically the remains of Buddha and other significant Buddhist figures.
 
• The relics are usually enclosed in a container and placed at the core of the stupa, symbolizing the Buddha's enlightened mind.
 
• Famous stupas like the **Sanchi Stupa in Madhya Pradesh** and the **Dhamek Stupa in Sarnath** hold significant historical and religious importance.
 
• Stupas are not only burial mounds but also serve as places of meditation and veneration for followers of Buddhism.
 
• The construction of stupas was initiated under the reign of Emperor **Ashoka**, who embraced Buddhism and propagated its teachings widely.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rock Edicts:**

 
 
• These are inscriptions on rocks and pillars issued by Emperor Ashoka, spreading messages of Dharma and Buddhism.
 
• They do not contain relics but are significant for understanding ancient Indian history and Ashoka’s rule.
 
 
 
• **Chaitya Halls:**
 
 
• Chaityas are Buddhist prayer halls with a stupa at one end, primarily used for congregational worship.
 
• Unlike stupas, chaityas are architectural spaces rather than reliquaries.
 
 
 
• **Ashokan Pillars:**
 
 
• These are monolithic columns erected by Emperor Ashoka, inscribed with edicts promoting Buddhist teachings and values.
 
• They do not enshrine relics but symbolize the propagation of Buddhism.
 
 
 
• **Types of Stupas:**
 
 
• Stupas are categorized into **relic stupas** (containing relics), **object stupas** (housing sacred objects), and **commemorative stupas** (marking significant events).
 
• Relic stupas are the most revered as they enshrine the physical remains of the Buddha or other enlightened beings.

questions.question: The present cost of a plot area is ₹1,12,079. After a year, its cost increased to ₹1,89,297. The percentage increase (rounded off to the nearest integer) in the cost of the plot area is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Approximate the values to the nearest thousands: 112k → 189k.

Increase ≈ 189 − 112 = 77.

Percentage Increase ≈ (77 ÷ 112) × 100.

77/112 ≈ 11/16 ≈ 68.75%.

**∴ The correct answer is 69%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Cost (CP) = ₹1,12,079

Final Cost (SP) = ₹1,89,297

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1a4381497b7915c350d4e9d79c33746c4dbdb6cbdb7eaf4c3e868cd687c100f5.png] 

**Formula:**

Percentage Increase = [(Final Cost − Initial Cost) ÷ Initial Cost] × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Increase = 1,89,297 − 1,12,079 = 77,218

⇒ Percentage Increase = (77,218 ÷ 1,12,079) × 100

⇒ Percentage Increase = 0.68895 × 100

⇒ Percentage Increase = 68.89% ≈ 69%

**∴ The correct answer is 69%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Change

It measures the degree of change over time. Formula: (Difference ÷ Original Value) × 100.

Rounding Off Rules

If the decimal part is 0.5 or greater, round up to the next integer. If less than 0.5, stay at the current integer.

Base Value Selection

Always use the **initial** or **original** value as the denominator when calculating percentage increase or decrease.

questions.question: The average age of Amit, Arjun and Anya is 30 years. If the average age of Amit and Anya is 35 years, what will be Arjun's age after 2 years?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total age of **Amit, Arjun, and Anya** = 30 × 3 = 90 years

Total age of **Amit and Anya** = 35 × 2 = 70 years

**Arjun's present age** = 90 − 70 = 20 years

**Arjun's age after 2 years** = 20 + 2 = 22 years

**∴ The correct answer is 22 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average age of **Amit, Arjun, and Anya** = 30 years

Average age of **Amit and Anya** = 35 years

**Formula Used:**

Total Sum = **Average × Number of observations**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/96e63e4789504190cc7edad8bbcd8ddef0add2d86e63172f4cd51cc6a9f6aa25.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total age of Amit, Arjun, and Anya = 30 × 3 = 90 years

⇒ Total age of Amit and Anya = 35 × 2 = 70 years

⇒ **Arjun's present age** = (Amit + Arjun + Anya) − (Amit + Anya)

⇒ Arjun's present age = 90 − 70 = 20 years

⇒ Arjun's age after 2 years = 20 + 2 = 22 years

**∴ The correct answer is 22 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Average Formula

Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Number of observations). To find the sum, use: **Sum = Average × Count**.

Age Increment Property

If the age of every person in a group increases by **n years**, the average age of the group also increases by **n years**.

Exclusion Principle

Age of excluded member = (Initial Sum) − (New Sum). This is used when one person leaves the group and the average changes.</p

questions.question: Which of the following farming techniques is primarily practised by tribal groups in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shifting agriculture**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Shifting agriculture**, also known as "slash-and-burn agriculture," is a traditional farming technique practised by tribal groups in India.
 
• In this method, patches of forest land are cleared by cutting and burning trees, and the land is used for cultivation until its fertility decreases.
 
• It is primarily practised in hilly and forested regions such as the northeastern states of India (e.g., Nagaland, Mizoram, and Manipur) and parts of Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, and Andhra Pradesh.
 
• Shifting agriculture is a subsistence farming method, meaning it is done primarily to meet the needs of the farmer's family rather than for commercial purposes.
 
• After a few years of cultivation, the land is left fallow for natural vegetation to grow back, which helps restore soil fertility.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Agriculture in India**

 
 
• **Commercial farming:** Involves large-scale production of crops for sale in markets (e.g., sugarcane, cotton).
 
• **Intensive farming:** High inputs of labor and capital are used on smaller plots of land to maximize output.
 
• **Plantation farming:** Large-scale cultivation of a single crop like tea, coffee, or rubber, typically for export.
 
 
 
• **Jhum Cultivation:** A specific form of shifting agriculture practised in northeastern India, where tribal farmers cultivate crops like rice, maize, and millets on cleared forest patches.
 
• **Environmental Concerns:** Shifting agriculture can lead to deforestation, soil erosion, and loss of biodiversity if not practised sustainably.
 
• **Government Initiatives:** Efforts are being made to introduce alternative livelihood options and sustainable farming practices for tribal communities to reduce the environmental impact of shifting agriculture.
 
• **Alternative Names:** Shifting agriculture is also referred to as "jhum," "podu," or "bewar" in different regions of India.

questions.question: A bank offers 7.4% compound interest per annum calculated on a half-yearly basis. A customer deposits ₹8,022 each on 1 January and 1 July of a year. At the end of the year, the amount he would have gained by way of interest is ______ (give your answer correct to 2 decimal places).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Half-yearly rate** (r) = 7.4% ÷ 2 = **3.7%**

Interest on 1st deposit (2 cycles) = 3.7 + 3.7 + (3.7 × 3.7)/100 = **7.5369%**

Interest on 2ⁿd deposit (1 cycle) = **3.7%**

**Total Interest %** = 7.5369% + 3.7% = **11.2369%**

Interest amount = 8022 × 11.2369 / 100 = **₹901.42**

**∴ The correct answer is ₹901.42.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = **₹8,022** for each deposit

Annual Rate (R) = **7.4%** | Time = **1 year**

Compounding = **Half-yearly**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/47108003f9aadb68d4fc6cea09cc14c1719293f8e1e9a7fa1cfaed4862b67712.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Compound Interest (CI) = P × [(1 + r/100)ⁿ − 1]

Where r = R/2 and n = number of half-years.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Half-yearly rate (r) = 7.4 ÷ 2 = 3.7%

⇒ **Interest on 1st deposit** (for 2 half-years):

⇒ I₁ = 8022 × [(1 + 3.7/100)² − 1]

⇒ I₁ = 8022 × [(1.037)² − 1] = 8022 × [1.075369 − 1]

⇒ I₁ = 8022 × 0.075369 = 604.610118

⇒ **Interest on 2ⁿd deposit** (for 1 half-year):

⇒ I₂ = 8022 × [3.7/100] = 8022 × 0.037

⇒ I₂ = 296.814

⇒ **Total Interest** = I₁ + I₂ = 604.610118 + 296.814

• HF (hydrofluoric acid) is classified as a weak acid because it does not completely dissociate into its ions in an aqueous solution.

• Since HF is a weak acid, its conjugate base (F⁻) has a relatively low tendency to accept protons, making it a **weak base**.

• These are pairs of molecules or ions that differ by a single proton (H⁺).

Ratio of **diagonals** = 8 : 15 → Half-diagonals = 4 : 7.5 → Side ratio = √(4² + 7.5²) = 8.5.

Comparing **side units**: 8.5 units = 25.5 cm ⇒ 1 unit = 3 cm.

Diagonals: d₁ = 8 × 3 = 24 cm, d₂ = 15 × 3 = 45 cm.

**Area** = (1 ÷ 2) × 24 × 45 = 12 × 45 = 540 cm².

⇒ 650.25 = 72.25x²

⇒ x² = 650.25 ÷ 72.25 = 9 ⇒ x = 3.

⇒ d₁ = 8 × 3 = 24 cm, d₂ = 15 × 3 = 45 cm.

⇒ Area = (1 ÷ 2) × 24 × 45 = 540 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 540 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Rhombus Diagonals

The diagonals of a **rhombus** bisect each other at **right angles** (90°), forming four congruent right-angled triangles.

Side and Diagonal Relationship

The relationship between side 'a' and diagonals 'd₁' and 'd₂' is given by the equation: 4a² = d₁² + d₂².

If the side 'a' and an internal angle 'θ' are known, **Area** = a² sin(θ).</p

questions.question: A boat takes 90 minutes to go 49.2 km upstream. The ratio of the speed of the boat in still water to that of the stream is 3 : 2. How much total time (in hours) will the boat take to go 44.8 km upstream and 71.2 km downstream?

**Upstream speed** (U) = 49.2 ÷ 1.5 = 32.8 kmph.

Ratio of **Speed in still water** (x) : **Speed of stream** (y) = 3 : 2.

Upstream ratio (x − y) = 3 − 2 = 1 unit → 32.8 kmph.

Downstream ratio (x + y) = 3 + 2 = 5 units → 5 × 32.8 = 164 kmph.

Total time = (44.8 ÷ 32.8) + (71.2 ÷ 164) = 1.365 + 0.434 ≈ 1.8 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.8 hours.**

⇒ Let x = 3k and y = 2k. Then U = x − y = 3k − 2k = k.

⇒ k = 32.8 kmph.

⇒ Speed Downstream (D) = x + y = 3k + 2k = 5k = 5 × 32.8 = 164 kmph.

⇒ Time for 44.8 km Upstream = 44.8 ÷ 32.8 = 1.3658... hours.

⇒ Time for 71.2 km Downstream = 71.2 ÷ 164 = 0.4341... hours.

Calculating x and y from U and D

Speed of Boat in Still Water (x) = (D + U) ÷ 2 and Speed of Stream (y) = (D − U) ÷ 2.</p

An **equivalent ratio** is obtained by **multiplying** or **dividing** both terms of the original ratio by the same **non-zero number**.

Equivalent Ratio Definition

Ratios that represent the same **proportion** between quantities are equivalent. They can be expressed as equal **fractions** (7/9 = 70/90).

Simplest Form

A ratio is in its **simplest form** if the HCF of its terms is 1. All equivalent ratios reduce to the same simplest form.</p

questions.question: The least number which, when diminished by 8, is divisible by 15, 12, 18 and 29 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **least number** is the **LCM** of (15, 12, 18, 29) + **diminished value**.

LCM(15, 12, 18, 29) → LCM(60, 18, 29) → LCM(180, 29).

Required number = (180 × 29) + 8 = 5220 + 8 = 5228.

**∴ The correct answer is 5228.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Divisors = 15, 12, 18, 29; Diminished value = 8.

**Formula Used:** Required Number = LCM(Divisors) + Remainder/Diminished value.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/08951313feb683cdea68db9b5e3c8f60a747aed1f26a05ed6fafdf72659a22e5.png] 

⇒ Prime factors of 15 = 3 × 5

⇒ Prime factors of 12 = 2² × 3

⇒ Prime factors of 18 = 2 × 3²

⇒ Prime factors of 29 = 29 (Prime number)

⇒ LCM = 2² × 3² × 5 × 29

⇒ LCM = 4 × 9 × 5 × 29 = 180 × 29 = 5220

⇒ Required number = 5220 + 8 = 5228

**∴ The correct answer is 5228.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM (Least Common Multiple)

The smallest positive integer that is divisible by each of the given numbers. Calculation: LCM(a, b) = (a × b) ÷ HCF(a, b).

Divisibility Rule for 9 (Special Case for 18)

If a number is divisible by 18, it must be divisible by 9. The sum of the digits of (5228 − 8) = 5+2+2+0 = 9, which is divisible by 9.

Prime Numbers

Numbers like 29 have no factors other than 1 and themselves; hence, they are multiplied directly in LCM calculations.</p

questions.question: A byke travels 80 km at the speed of 40 km/hr and the next 45 km at the speed of 15 km/hr. What is its average speed (in km/hr)?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
**Average Speed** = **Total Distance** ÷ **Total Time**

Time 1 = 80 ÷ 40 = 2 hours

Time 2 = 45 ÷ 15 = 3 hours

Average Speed = (80 + 45) ÷ (2 + 3) = 125 ÷ 5 = 25 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 25 km/hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance₁ (d₁) = 80 km, Speed₁ (s₁) = 40 km/hr

Distance₂ (d₂) = 45 km, Speed₂ (s₂) = 15 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Average Speed = (Total Distance) ÷ (Total Time)
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/62d82559a7f63e1ccf3f8b0c1acf32d0d7f723cf099766f1e198131da2f47c29.png] 
⇒ Total Distance = 80 + 45 = 125 km

⇒ Time taken for first part (t₁) = 80 ÷ 40 = 2 hours

⇒ Time taken for second part (t₂) = 45 ÷ 15 = 3 hours

⇒ Total Time = 2 + 3 = 5 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 125 ÷ 5 = 25 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 25 km/hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Equal Distance Case

If a journey covers two equal distances at speeds u and v, then Average Speed = (2 × u × v) ÷ (u + v).

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, relative speed is the difference of their speeds. In opposite directions, it is the sum.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.</p

__
 
• **Narasimhavarman II**, also known as Rajasimha, was a Pallava ruler who reigned during the late 7th and early 8th century CE.
 
• He is credited with the construction of the iconic **Shore Temple** at Mahabalipuram, which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• The Shore Temple is one of the earliest structural temples built using granite and represents the zenith of Pallava architecture.
 
• Narasimhavarman II's reign saw significant advancements in art, architecture, and cultural development in South India.
 
• The temple complex showcases a blend of Shaivism and Vaishnavism, with shrines dedicated to Lord Shiva and Lord Vishnu.

• The Pallavas were a prominent South Indian dynasty that ruled between the 3rd and 9th centuries CE.
 
• They were known for their patronage of art, architecture, and literature, with Mahabalipuram being a significant center of their cultural heritage.
 
• Key rulers include Mahendravarman I, Narasimhavarman I (Mamallan), and Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha).

• Located in Tamil Nadu, Mahabalipuram is famous for its rock-cut sculptures and structural temples.

• South Indian temples are known for their distinctive Dravidian architectural style.
 
• Features include gopurams (tower gateways), vimanas (temple towers), and intricate carvings depicting deities and mythological stories.
 
• The Pallavas contributed significantly to the development of structural temple architecture, transitioning from rock-cut to granite-built temples.

questions.question: Which of the following could be the factors that led Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) to withdraw significant funds from Indian equities according to the Economic Survey 2024-25? 1. Slowing earnings growth 2. High valuations 3. Rising geopolitical tensions

• The **Economic Survey 2024-25** highlights multiple factors that could have influenced the withdrawal of Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) from Indian equities.
 
• **Slowing earnings growth**: Reduced corporate earnings impact investor confidence, leading to lower equity investments.
 
• **High valuations**: Overvaluation of Indian stocks relative to other emerging markets or global benchmarks can deter FPIs.
 
• **Rising geopolitical tensions**: Escalating global or regional uncertainties (e.g., conflicts, trade wars) often make investors shift funds to safer markets.
 
• The combination of these factors heightens market risk and makes Indian equities less attractive compared to other investment destinations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• FPIs include investments in stocks, bonds, or other financial assets in a foreign country without obtaining significant ownership.
 
• Such investments are more volatile and sensitive to economic, political, and market conditions.
 
 
 
• **High Valuations:**
 
 
• Stock valuations are often measured using indicators like the Price-to-Earnings (P/E) ratio.
 
• Overvaluation occurs when stock prices are excessively higher than their actual earnings potential.
 
 
 
• **Geopolitical Tensions:**
 
 
• These refer to conflicts or uncertainties between nations that may disrupt global trade, investments, and market stability.
 
• Examples include trade wars, sanctions, or military escalations.
 
 
 
• **Impact of FPI Outflows:**
 
 
• Significant withdrawal of FPIs can weaken the domestic currency due to reduced capital inflows.
 
• It can also lead to stock market volatility and reduced liquidity.

• It provides a detailed review of the economic developments in India during the past financial year.

questions.question: What was the main purpose of the citadel in Harappan cities?

options.text: To function as a residential area
To organise administrative and public functions

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The citadel in Harappan cities was primarily used for administrative and public functions, indicating a well-organized urban planning system.
 
• Structures within the citadel, such as granaries and assembly halls, suggest it served as the hub for governance, storage, and possibly trade regulation.
 
• Archaeological evidence, such as the Great Bath in Mohenjo-daro, highlights that the citadel also hosted significant public events and rituals.
 
• Its elevated position was likely strategic, offering protection from floods and enhancing its importance within the city layout.
 
• The citadel reflects the Harappan civilization's advanced socio-political organization and ability to manage large-scale infrastructure projects.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Urban Planning in Harappan Civilization:**

 
 
• Harappan cities were divided into two parts: the citadel (higher ground) and the lower town (residential and commercial areas).
 
• Drainage systems, grid-like street layouts, and standardized brick sizes showcase their advanced planning.
 
 
 
• **The Great Bath:**
 
 
• Located in Mohenjo-daro, the Great Bath is one of the most remarkable structures of the Harappan civilization.
 
• It is believed to have been used for ritualistic bathing, reflecting the importance of water in their culture.
 
 
 
• **Granaries:**
 
 
• Large granaries were found in Harappan cities, indicating centralized storage and distribution of food grains.
 
• This reflects the civilization's ability to manage agricultural surplus and address food security.
 
 
 
• **Decline of the Harappan Civilization:**
 
 
• Factors such as climate change, tectonic shifts, and changes in river systems (e.g., drying of the Saraswati River) are believed to have contributed to its decline.
 
• The disappearance of centralized administration disrupted the urban structure of Harappan cities.

questions.question: If the sum of two numbers p and m is 12 and (p ^ 3 + m ^ 3) = 360 then find the value of pm.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct identity: **p³ + m³ = (p + m)³ − 3pm(p + m)**

Substitute the given values: 360 = 12³ − 3pm(12)

360 = 1728 − 36pm

36pm = 1728 − 360 = 1368

pm = 1368 ÷ 36 = 38

**∴ The correct answer is 38.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sum of two numbers (p + m) = 12

Sum of their cubes (p³ + m³) = 360

**Formula Used:**

Algebraic identity: (a + b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3ab(a + b)

**Calculations:**

⇒ (p + m)³ = p³ + m³ + 3pm(p + m)

⇒ (12)³ = 360 + 3 × pm × 12

⇒ 1728 = 360 + 36pm

⇒ 36pm = 1728 − 360

⇒ 36pm = 1368

⇒ pm = 1368 ÷ 36

⇒ pm = 38

**∴ The correct answer is 38.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Cubes Factorization

The identity a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²) can also be used to find the sum of cubes.

Difference of Cubes Identity

For subtraction, the identity is a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²).

Algebraic Relationships

Using p + m and pm, one can also find p² + m² using (p + m)² − 2pm.</p

questions.question: A shopkeeper sold a book for ₹544 at a loss of 36%. At what price (in ₹) should he sell it to gain 24% on it?

Ratio of **Selling Prices** is equivalent to the ratio of (100 − **Loss%**) and (100 + **Gain%**).

Initial SP : New SP = (100 − 36) : (100 + 24) = 64 : 124.

Given: 64 units = ₹544 ⇒ 1 unit = 544 ÷ 64 = 8.5.

New SP = 124 × 8.5 = ₹1,054.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,054.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial SP = ₹544, Loss = 36%, Desired Gain = 24%.

questions.question: Two numbers are in the ratio 7 : 11. If the first number is increased by 10 and the second number is decreased by 20, then the ratio becomes 2 : 3. What is the sum of the original two numbers?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Initial Ratio = 7 : 11 (Sum = 18 units)

Final Ratio = 2 : 3

Applying **Cross Multiplication Method**:

(7 × 3) − (11 × 2) units = (2 × −20) − (3 × 10)

|21 − 22| units = |−40 − 30| ⇒ 1 unit = 70

Sum of original numbers = 18 × 70 = 1260

**∴ The correct answer is 1260.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6d616a394ce1c4aa7d271945906a753d77f00ca2e0ad75b3fed3dcaa81a0511d.png] 

**Given:** Ratio of two numbers = 7 : 11

**Let:** First number = 7x and Second number = 11x

According to the question:

⇒ (7x + 10) / (11x − 20) = 2 / 3

⇒ 3 × (7x + 10) = 2 × (11x − 20)

⇒ 21x + 30 = 22x − 40

⇒ 22x − 21x = 30 + 40

⇒ x = 70

⇒ First number = 7 × 70 = 490

⇒ Second number = 11 × 70 = 770

⇒ Sum of original numbers = 490 + 770 = 1260

**∴ The correct answer is 1260.**

**__Additional Information__**

Ratio and Proportion

A **Ratio** is a comparison of two quantities. If a : b = c : d, then ad = bc (Product of Extremes = Product of Means).

Cross-Multiplication Technique

Used when a fixed value is added/subtracted from ratio terms to get a new ratio. It avoids **algebraic variables** and saves time in exams.

Sum of Ratio Parts

If the original ratio is a : b, the **sum of numbers** will always be a multiple of (a + b). Here, 1260 is a multiple of (7 + 11 = 18).</p

Find the circumference (in m) of the largest circle that can be inscribed in a rectangle whose dimensions are given as 281 m and 133 m.

{Take } pi = (22)/(7)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **diameter** of the largest **inscribed circle** in a **rectangle** is always equal to the **shorter side**.

Diameter (d) = 133 m

Circumference = π × d = (22/7) × 133

Circumference = 22 × 19 = 418 m

**∴ The correct answer is 418 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of **rectangle** (L) = 281 m

Breadth of **rectangle** (B) = 133 m

**Formula Used:**

Circumference of a **circle** = 2πr = πd

Diameter of the **inscribed circle** = min(L, B)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/76a86aed51da3f03bad1c42d8ab9f2f8a775937237287db32758b9461a16d61b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ For the **circle** to fit inside the **rectangle**, its **diameter** cannot exceed the **smallest dimension**.

⇒ Diameter (d) = 133 m

⇒ Circumference = π × d

⇒ Circumference = (22/7) × 133

⇒ Circumference = 22 × 19

⇒ Circumference = 418 m

**∴ The correct answer is 418 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Inscribed Circle

The **area** of the largest **circle** in a **rectangle** is πr², where r = Breadth/2.

Circle Inscribed in a Square

For a **square** of side 'a', the **diameter** of the **inscribed circle** is exactly equal to 'a'.

Circumscribed Circle

The **diameter** of a **circle** circumscribing a **rectangle** is equal to the **diagonal** of the **rectangle** (√(L²+B²)).</p

questions.question: When was the discovery of salvarsan recognised with a Nobel Prize in Medicine?

__
 
• The discovery of **Salvarsan (arsphenamine)**, the first effective treatment for syphilis, was made by **Paul Ehrlich and his team** in 1907.
 
• Paul Ehrlich was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1908**, shared with Ilya Mechnikov, for their work on immunity.
 
• The Nobel Prize recognized Ehrlich's groundbreaking contributions, including the development of Salvarsan and his "magic bullet" concept for targeted therapies.
 
• Salvarsan is considered a significant milestone in the history of chemotherapy and the treatment of infectious diseases.
 
• The discovery marked the beginning of the use of synthetic drugs to combat microbial infections.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Salvarsan (Arsphenamine):**

 
 
• It was the first synthetic antimicrobial drug used to treat syphilis, a bacterial infection caused by Treponema pallidum.
 
• The drug belongs to the arsenic compound class and was a precursor to modern antibiotics.
 
• Salvarsan was introduced into medical practice in 1910 and was considered revolutionary for its time.
 
 
 
• **Paul Ehrlich:**
 
 
• A German physician and scientist known as the "Father of Chemotherapy."
 
• He developed the "magic bullet" theory, envisioning drugs that could specifically target disease-causing organisms without harming the host.
 
• His work laid the foundation for modern pharmacology and immunology.
 
 
 
• **Nobel Prize in 1908:**
 
 
• The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1908 was awarded jointly to Paul Ehrlich and Ilya Mechnikov.
 
• Ilya Mechnikov's contribution involved the discovery of phagocytosis, a key mechanism of innate immunity.
 
• Their combined work advanced the understanding of immunological responses and therapeutic interventions.
 
 
 
• **Syphilis:**
 
 
• A sexually transmitted infection caused by the bacterium Treponema pallidum.
 
• Symptoms include sores, rashes, and, in severe cases, damage to organs and the nervous system.
 
• Before Salvarsan, syphilis was treated with mercury compounds, which were highly toxic and ineffective.

questions.question: In 2024, the Indian government approved defence acquisitions worth $17.3 billion. How much percentage of these acquisitions was sourced from domestic suppliers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**99%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In 2024, the Indian government approved defence acquisitions worth $17.3 billion to strengthen national security and bolster defence capabilities.
 
• Out of the total approved acquisitions, only **99%** was sourced from domestic suppliers, reflecting a focus on international procurement for advanced technologies.
 
• This highlights the continued reliance on foreign suppliers for high-tech military equipment despite government initiatives to promote indigenous defence manufacturing.
 
• India has launched policies like **‘Make in India’** and Defence Production and Export Promotion Policy (DPEPP) to boost domestic production, but challenges in scaling technology remain.
 
• The low percentage underscores the need for further investment and development in domestic defence industries to reduce dependency on imports.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Make in India Initiative**

 
 
• Launched in September 2014, it aims to transform India into a global manufacturing hub.
 
• Encourages investments in 25 sectors, including defence manufacturing.
 
• Focuses on reducing imports and increasing domestic production capabilities.
 
 
 
• **Defence Production and Export Promotion Policy (DPEPP) 2020**
 
 
• Aims to achieve a turnover of Rs. 1,75,000 crore ($25 billion) in defence manufacturing by 2025.
 
• Focuses on increasing exports to Rs. 35,000 crore ($5 billion) by 2025.
 
• Promotes self-reliance in defence production by encouraging private sector participation.
 
 
 
• **Offset Policy in Defence Procurement**
 
 
• Introduced to leverage foreign defence procurement for domestic capabilities.
 
• Mandates foreign suppliers to invest a percentage of the contract value in Indian industries.
 
• Helps promote technology transfer and industrial collaboration.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Indigenous Defence Manufacturing**
 
 
• Limited access to advanced technologies and research capabilities.
 
• High dependence on foreign collaborations for critical components.
 
• Need for policy reforms to streamline procurement and production processes.
